items.title: Largest BESS in Czech Republic commissioned, supplied by CATL-backed CNTE
items.summary: The largest grid-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) project in the Czech Republic has gone online, supplied by a company invested in by lithium-ion OEM CATL.

items.title: Massachusetts issues RFP seeking 1,000MW of BESS

items.title: China draws a line under the solar price war
items.summary: Regulators in China are calling on domestic manufacturers to end destructive below-cost competition but are yet to impose a formal price floor. The post China draws a line under the solar price war appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: Romania’s solar capacity exceeds 8.5 GW
items.summary: Romania's solar market continues to grow with around 1.8 GW installed since the start of the year. The country appears on track to reach its current 2030 target of 10 GW as early as next year. The post Romania’s solar capacity exceeds 8.5 GW appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.summary: Analysis by the Pakistan Solar Association finds roughly 51 TWh of generation that never appears on grid-side data, as rooftop and off-grid solar spreads faster than official statistics. items.title: Prosalia and EDP hybridise solar PV/wind projects with batteries in Portugal, Spain
items.summary: IPP Prosalia has commissioned a 15MW/60MWh battery storage system at a solar PV plant in Portugal, while power group EDP has added one to a hybrid wind and solar project in Spain.

items.title: European multi-day energy storage startup Ore Energy raises US$43 million in Series A
items.summary: Iron-air battery company Ore Energy has raised US$43 million in a Series A funding round to commercialise its multi-day energy storage technology.

items.title: Researchers design PVT heat pump with single integrated evaporator
items.summary: The dual-source photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) heat pump combines solar and ambient-air heat collection in a single finned evaporator, eliminating the need for separate heat exchangers. items.title: Clean energy offers least-cost path to meeting US electricity demand
items.summary: Study by the Electricity and Energy Innovation finds choosing a clean energy pathway to meeting America's electricity demand in 2030 would cost $5 billion less than meeting the demand with fossil fuels The post Clean energy offers least-cost path to meeting US electricity demand appeared first on pv magazine Global .

items.title: Photovoltaics feed record 12 TWh into Germany’s public grid in July

items.summary: The proposal aims to fill a capacity shortfall driven by surging data center demand, which could grow by 70 GW by 2038, according to the PJM Interconnection. The success of the plan depends on states taking steps to protect their retail customers from cost shifts, it said.
